scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

On Thursday, she texted after work to say she was on her way, but her ex said they weren't home. They argued, and she suggested switching weekends so she could have her makeup time. Her ex refused. Now, her weekend is coming up, and she's not getting him at the regular time because he's at an amusement park with her family. She's expected to give up even more of her time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. She's asking if she's the asshole for putting her foot down and keeping her son during their family function so she can enjoy time with him during her scheduled time. So, is she ITA? Let's think about the factors. 1. Custody arrangement: Legally, she has every other weekend and a weekday. That's what the court decided, so it's a legal agreement. She's supposed to follow that unless there's a court order change. 2. Her accommodating nature: She's been flexible, allowing her ex to change the schedule for activities, family, or the son's feelings. But now she's putting her foot down. 3. The specific incident: She agreed to let the son stay with his mother last Wednesday, but then wanted him on Thursday. Her ex took him to the lake, and they argued. She suggested switching weekends, which her ex refused. Now, during her scheduled time, the son is with her ex's family, and she's not getting him. 4. Her perspective: She feels she's been accommodating but now is standing her ground to have her scheduled time with her son. She's not willing to give up more time. 5. Her ex's perspective: She's using the son as an excuse, and the ex is trying to have fun with the son, possibly feeling that the woman is being too rigid. Now, considering whether she's ITA. The key points are: - She's following the legal custody arrangement, which is her right. - She's been accommodating but now is asserting her scheduled time. - Her ex is using the son's activities as a reason to keep him, possibly taking advantage of her flexibility. Is it wrong for her to stand her ground? Or is she being reasonable in enforcing the custody agreement? I think it's reasonable for her to enforce the custody arrangement, especially since she's been flexible in the past. It's important for both parents to respect the court-ordered schedule to provide stability for the child. If one parent constantly changes the schedule, it can lead to resentment and instability. However, communication is key. She could have approached the situation more calmly, perhaps discussing the issue without arguing. But given the history, it's understandable she's frustrated. So, is she ITA? I don't think so. She's asserting her legal right to spend time with her son as per the court order. It's not asshole behavior; it's standing up for herself and her son's best interests in terms of a stable schedule.
